channel.title: Food Safety Magazine - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Food Safety Magazine (food-safety.com)

item.title: FDA’s Human Foods Program Publishes Priority Scientific Needs to Advance Food Safety
item.description: The list of data, method, and research needs spans microbiological and chemical safety, nutrition, risk assessment, and other areas. It is intended to guide researchers who are interested in pursuing impactful food safety research.

item.title: Codex Committee Advances Work on Standards for Veterinary Drug Residues in Food
item.description: The 28th session of the Codex Committee on Residues of Veterinary Drugs in Foods made advances related to maximum residue limits (MRLs), extrapolation approaches, and risk management guidance, with several measures forwarded to the Codex Alimentarius Commission for adoption.

item.title: Center for Food Safety Opposes Monsanto–Bayer Legal Efforts to Preempt State Pesticide Warnings
item.description: Arguing that states’ authority to require pesticide health warnings is critical to filling gaps in EPA oversight and risk communication, a coalition has filed an amicus brief in the U.S. Supreme Court case Monsanto v. Durnell, in which Monsanto (now Bayer), the maker of glyphosate-based Roundup, seeks to strike down that authority.

item.title: Mississippi Bans Cell-Cultured Milk Products, Sets Label Restrictions for Alternative ‘Meat’ Products
item.description: Effective July 1, HB 1153 bans the sale of milk products produced through cell-culturing and sets forth labeling requirements for products containing cell-based, insect-based, or plant-based protein.

item.title: Raw Farm Recalls Unpasteurized Cheese While Denying Link to E. coli Outbreak
item.description: The company says the recall is being issued “under protest” and “as a path forward,” while continuing to contest the epidemiological evidence provided by FDA.

item.title: U.S. Codex Office to Hold Public Meeting Ahead of CCFL49
item.description: The objective of the virtual public meeting is to provide information and receive public comments on agenda items and draft U.S. positions to be discussed at the upcoming 49th Session of the Codex Committee on Food Labeling (CCFL49).

item.title: Food Innovation: An Introduction to Precision Fermentation
item.description: Precision fermentation has the potential to improve food security, promote sustainable food production, and support the food sector as an important driver of economic growth. The biotechnology behind precision fermentation is likely to become progressively visible, and its role in food manufacturing will become increasingly important.

item.title: Testing Confirms Microbiological, Chemical Safety of Canadian Infant Formula, Children’s Foods
item.description: The Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) recently published the findings from several food sampling and testing assignments for microbiological and chemical contaminants across a range of food categories. In general, the results were satisfactory.

item.title: SafetyChain Unveils Updates to Digital Plant Management Platform
item.description: The new functionality is aimed at improving information flow, visibility, and coordination across frontline food safety and quality operations.

item.title: Stop Foodborne Illness, FDA to Host ‘Culture Change Carnival’ Webinar in April
item.description: The free event is open to the public and is the fifth installment in the joint multi-part webinar series focused on advancing food safety culture.

item.title: Food Safety Five Ep. 29: The ‘Dirty Dozen’ Debate—Pesticides in Produce Explained
item.description: This episode of Food Safety Five discusses the Environmental Working Group’s 2026 “Dirty Dozen” list of the most “pesticide-contaminated produce,” including ongoing debate over the list’s methodology and its relevance to food safety and public health.

item.title: CRISPR-Edited Wheat Leads to Reduced Acrylamide Without Yield Loss
item.description: Rothamsted Research scientists have developed gene-edited wheat with substantially reduced levels of free asparagine, a precursor to acrylamide. Biscuits produced from gene-edited wheat showed a 93 percent reduction in acrylamide compared to controls.

item.title: Eurofins Supplement Certification Enters SuppCo TrustScore Rating System
item.description: SuppCo’s mobile application evaluates dietary supplements using its TrustScore methodology. Eurofins Supplement Testing and the Eurofins Assurance provide testing services and certification programs for dietary supplements and ingredients.

item.title: MicroPure Introduces Manifolds for Culinary Steam Filtration in Food Processing
item.description: The steam manifolds are delivered fully assembled and include MicroPure filters, housings, condensate traps, lockable isolation valves, and upstream and downstream pressure gauges.

item.title: Monitoring and Recordkeeping: The Heart of HACCP
item.description: Monitoring and recordkeeping are the heart of HACCP. Records demonstrate that the program is being properly managed and that the established critical limits are being met, providing supporting data to show that the processor is producing safe foods.
